questions.question: What is the root cause of all fundamental economic problems?

options.label: B
options.text: Scarcity of resources relative to unlimited human wants

questions.correct_answer_text: Scarcity of resources relative to unlimited human wants
questions.explanation: Human wants are unlimited while productive economic resources are strictly finite and scarce.

questions.question: Who defined Economics as 'the study of mankind in the ordinary business of life'?
questions.explanation: Alfred Marshall provided the welfare definition of economics in his 1890 book 'Principles of Economics'.

questions.question: Opportunity cost is defined as:

options.label: A
options.text: The monetary cost of buying goods

options.label: B
options.text: The value of the next best alternative forgone

options.label: D
options.text: The sunk cost of past investments

questions.correct_answer_text: The value of the next best alternative forgone
questions.explanation: Opportunity cost represents the sacrifice of the highest-valued forgone choice when a decision is made.

questions.question: Points lying inside a Production Possibility Curve (PPC) indicate:
questions.explanation: Points inside the PPC show that society is producing below its potential due to idle capacity or unemployment.

questions.question: In a market (capitalist) economic system, fundamental economic questions are resolved by:

options.label: B
options.text: Price mechanism (forces of demand and supply)

questions.correct_answer_text: Price mechanism (forces of demand and supply)
questions.explanation: Adam Smith's 'invisible hand' or free market price mechanism guides resource allocation in capitalism.
